chapter: Ellington, the South, bebop and radio
title: Variety in radio: country, rock and roll and the rest
summary: Country and rock are fine but he objects to hearing one type constantly and wishes radio gave variety.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, there are a few stations that are a little different. But the dominant thing is just one thing, yes.
Even though, you know, they tried recently, and they've been doing it for a while now...but bringing Country Music into...

That's all right, too. And so is Rock-and-Roll. But don't play nothin' but Rock-and-Roll. [SINGS FIFTIES JUMP REFRAIN LOUDLY] I mean, you know, it's all right to do it once or twice. But not every number. It's going to be fast, it's going to be slow, but it's going to be the same...generally the same things. Why don't they vary it?

And don't play too much of any type, but give everybody a chance to hear something. Some people like to hear pretty music, beautiful music, you know. I can stand listening to any type of music played once, one piece, one thing. But if you're going to keep cramming it down my throat, every number I hear is the same thing, I'm going to turn that off.
